body:
I think references to the fact that one can perform penetration testing against L1 requirements should be removed.  Here is a quick look at what can't be penetration tested automatically at L1 (if it requires manual penetration testing, I added a requires manual next to it).  I didn't cover all of them and there are others.  My point is just that a lot of requirements require more than just a penetration test.

- 1.1
- 2.2
- 2.13
- 2.27 (possibly)
- 2.32 (might not be accessible to penetration testers.  Also, automated tools can't pick this up)
- 2.42
- 3.5 (requires manual)
- 3.19 (requires manual)
- 4.1 (can't be automated unless you are given a list of these)
- 4.4 (requires manual)
- 4.9 (requires manual)
- 4.16
- 4.17
- 5.3
- 5.6
- 5.15 (requires manual for DOM XSS, etc.)
- 5.29 (requires manual)
- 7 (basically all of them require access to source code)
- 8 (basically all of them require access to source code)
- 9.2
- 9.4 (requires manual)
- 9.6
- etc.

comments.body: I think L1 should become an "essential" list of CVSS v3 > 6.0 items. That way, we can target high value from an objective point of view.
